title: UK CPI, March 2027 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the last zero-rated collection month, and on the April-2026 analogue the exact day the April MPR's conditioning window closes
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/consumerpriceinflationukmarch2027, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the ONS release-calendar entry reads verbatim 'Consumer price inflation, UK: March 2027', 'Provisional release date: 21 April 2027 7:00am', and 'This release is not yet published'. The 07:00 London clock is the ONS's own on the same page and matches every prior bulletin in the series. Filed estimate on the ONS's own 'provisional' label, on this lane's no-self-confirm limit, and on the taxonomy gap that market-events-data.ts's confirmed prefixes cover no foreign national statistics institute — the same basis as uk-cpi-2026-12-16 and uk-cpi-2027-05-19. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of boe-decision-2027-04-29, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED BY THE boe-decision-2027-04-29 LANE, 2026-09-09, for two reasons neither of which is 'the next CPI print'. FIRST, IT IS THE LAST ZERO-RATED COLLECTION MONTH. SI 2026/987 zero-rates GB domestic electricity 'for supplies made in the period beginning with 1st October 2026 and ending with 31st March 2027' (legislation.gov.uk, fetched by the uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01 lane 2026-09-09). ONS collects prices around the Tuesday nearest the 13th, so the MARCH 2027 collection sits inside the window and this print still carries the full drag; the APRIL print on 2027-05-19 is the first observation of the reversion. A reader comparing the two without knowing that will read a tax step as re-acceleration. SECOND, AND THIS IS WHY IT IS PROPOSED BY A CENTRAL-BANK LANE RATHER THAN A CPI ONE: on the exact April analogue it lands ON the day the Monetary Policy Report's conditioning window closes. The April 2026 MPR ('Published on 30 April 2026', BoE primary fetched 2026-09-09) conditions its projections on 'the 15 days to 22 April' — and the ONS March 2026 CPI bulletin was released 22 April 2026. The same 8-day gap applied to the 2027-04-29 MPR puts its cut-off on 2027-04-21, this date; the July 2026 MPR's 10-day gap ('the 15 working days to 20 July' for a 30 July publication) puts the plausible band at 2027-04-19 to 2027-04-21. So this print is either inside the published forecast's market path by a single session or just outside it, and which of the two is a fact the April 2027 MPR itself will state. That is the observation that scores FT-boe-decision-2027-04-29-1. Tiered low to match uk-cpi-2026-12-16 and the rest of the uk-cpi series; symbols: [], no house playbook is UK- or sterling-keyed, and estimate widens caution only.
